title: Hotfix & Rollback Operational Playbook: branching, severity gates, and automated backporting
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Objective: Produce an operationally prescriptive playbook and small set of automation helpers for fast, low-risk hotfix rollouts and rollbacks across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments. This ticket delivers: a severity classification matrix, standardized patch-branch naming and backport policy, non-blocking rollout gates (canary + metric thresholds), an automated helper to create backport branches and PRs, and an updated rollback runbook for on-call use.

Scope and deliverables:
- Severity matrix (sev0/sev1/sev2) tuned for inference platform specifics (model-serving regression, token-cost spikes, SLO breaches, security incidents).
- Branching policy: canonical patch branch format, branch protection rules, and a lightweight backport script that creates per-target-branch PRs with changelog + test matrix.
- Backport strategy: which minor/patch branches get backports (LTS channels), policy for skipping backports with rationale, and automated labeling for triage.
- Rollout gates: define metric-driven gates (error-rate, p95 latency, failed-requests-per-minute, model-quality regression) and tolerances per channel (hosted vs. dedicated vs. private).
- Rollback playbook: single-command rollback for runtime-service, fallback model-routing, and cross-region traffic migration play steps.
- Automation: implement a CLI script (redwood-hotfix) to scaffold patch branch, open PRs against targeted channels, wire CI jobs for smoke checks, and optionally create an emergency release tag.
- Observability links: dashboards and SLO checks to be included in PR checklists and on-call paging rules.

Severity criteria (summary):
- SEV0 (P0): Production-wide model-serving correctness regression or data-exfiltration. Immediate pager, emergency patch branch, immediate rollback allowed. Backport to all supported LTS channels.
- SEV1 (P0/P1): Major degradation (p95 latency > SLO x1.5, request errors > 3x baseline sustained 5m), or severe cost amplification. Rapid hotfix and canary roll; backport to current active branches decided by engineering lead.
- SEV2 (P2): Localized or non-critical regressions (single region, minor quality drop). Work in normal cycle with scheduled patch; optional backport to next patch release.

Branching and naming conventions (must-follow):
- Patch branch format: hotfix/ENG-<ticket>-<short-desc>-<target> (e.g., hotfix/ENG-32801-kvcache-fix-runtime-1.19).
- Backport PR titles: [backport to runtime-1.18] <orig PR title> (automatically add label backport-required or backport-skip).
- Tagging: release-hotfix/<runtime-version>-<date>-<counter>.

Backport automation behavior:
- Script will accept a list of target branches and run the following steps: create branch from target, cherry-pick commits (with conflict detection), run CI smoke matrix, open draft PR with checklist and prefilled reviewers (release engineers + on-call). Conflicts escalate to assignee for manual resolution.
- If conflict-free, PR will be auto-marked for expedited review and merged with a fast-merge pipeline that runs the minimal runtime smoke tests and deployment gating.

Rollout gates and canary policy:
- Canary size: default 5% traffic on hosted; for Dedicated default 1 node; for Private follow customer-configured canary nodes.
- Gate metrics: new-error-rate <= baseline + 0.1% absolute AND p95 latency <= baseline * 1.2 AND model-quality regression <= 2% (if evaluators available).
- Auto-fail: any SEV0 condition or critical security alert triggers immediate abort and rollback.

Rollback runbook highlights (on-call friendly):
- One-line rollback: redwood-admin rollback --service runtime --to-tag <previous-stable-tag> --reason "<incidentsummary>". This triggers automatic rerouting of model variants and invalidates new KV cache shards.
- Post-rollback checks: validate traffic distribution, SLOs stable within 10 minutes, run a sample of production prompts through canary model, and create postmortem stub.
- Communication: update incident channel, create hotfix ticket with linked rollback PR and postmortem, and notify affected customers (for Dedicated/Private).

Review and governance:
- All hotfix PRs require sign-off from a release engineer and product owner for customer-impacting changes.
- Security-impacting fixes additionally require security team sign-off (manual or expedited SSO flow).

Open trade-offs and decisions to document:
- Aggressive auto-backport vs. conservative manual backport: initial implementation will auto-open backport PRs but not auto-merge unless safety checks pass. This balances speed with correctness.
- Canary size standardization: using percentage-based canaries works for Hosted but is less appropriate for Dedicated — we will maintain dual defaults and include guidance.

Acceptance criteria:
- Severity matrix published in Confluence and linked from README.
- redwood-hotfix CLI implemented with ability to scaffold and open backport PRs for at least two target branches.
- Rollback CLI path validated end-to-end in the staging environment and exercised by on-call in a fire-drill.
- PR template and CI checks updated to include required observability links and gating thresholds.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: automatic cherry-picks cause subtle regressions across runtime permutations. Mitigation: require CI smoke matrix and manual reviewer on conflicts.
- Risk: rollback may not clear in-flight KV cache leading to inconsistent outputs. Mitigation: include an explicit KV cache invalidation step as part of rollback and ensure compatibility tests for cache clearing.

Artifacts (to be created or updated):
- Confluence doc: "Hotfix & Rollback Playbook" (link below).
- GitHub helper repo: redwood/release-tools redwood-hotfix PR (draft).
- Runbook: runtime-rollback-runbook (playbook entry updated).
- Dashboards: runtime/hotfix-gates dashboard and runtime/rolling-deploys SLO deck.

Notes: This ticket bridges the operational and developer experience sides of release engineering—expect close collaboration with SRE, Runtime, Product, and Security. The implementation will be iterative; the first tranche focuses on clarity and safe automation for the most common paths.
